title: feat(radio): a command to deliver the held backlog, so a queued task needs no adhoc re-push
description:
## what

add a command that delivers the held radio backlog on its own — e.g. `rhx radio.task.push --held` or `rhx radio.task.held --deliver` — with no new task required.

## why

today a held task leaves only one way out: "the next push that gets through delivers the backlog first". so to deliver a task already queued, a clone must push it again by hand — rebuild its title and description from the held record, pipe them back in, and lean on `--idem findsert` to avoid a duplicate. that is adhoc, error-prone (a hand-copied title can drift from the record), and it reaches for a create when the intent is a flush.

`radio.task.held` already shows what waits and who can lift the gate. the act that should follow it — "the gate is open now, send what waits" — has no command.

## evidence

`ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-ehmpathy`, 2026-10-08: a task held since 2026-10-07 (`radio.uses:blocked — global`) waited after the human lifted the global block. to deliver it, the clone read `record.<key>.json`, copied its description into a file, and re-ran `radio.task.push --title '<same title>' --description @stdin --idem findsert` (delivered as ehmpathy/rhachet#586).

## shape

1. a flush command: deliver every QUEUED record in `$route/.radio/` (or `.behavior/.radio/`), oldest first, under the same gate check a push runs; report delivered / still held per task, with the exid
2. idempotent: a re-run after a full flush reports `backlog = 0` and creates naught
3. one record that faults on its own input (not the network) is named and skipped, so the rest still flow (see ehmpathy/rhachet-roles-bhuild#450, where one bad title held the queue)
4. `radio.task.held` names the command in its hint, in place of "the next push delivers the backlog"
